original_text:
X-Linked Inheritance
It was strange to Morgan’s team that even though the inheritance followed the 3:1 of regular autosomal dominance, only males ever had white eyes!Males that express a trait because they only receive one copy are called Hemizygous
explanation: During their fruit fly experiments, Thomas Hunt Morgan's team noticed that while eye color inheritance followed a general 3:1 dominant-to-recessive ratio, only male flies expressed the white-eyed phenotype. This occurred because the eye color gene is X-linked. Because males only have a single X chromosome (XY), they have only one copy of X-linked genes. Males are therefore called hemizygous for these traits, meaning any recessive allele on their single X chromosome will be expressed.

questions.q: What term describes males who express X-linked recessive traits because they only have a single X chromosome?
questions.exp: Option C is correct because the slide defines: 'Males that express a trait because they only receive one copy are called Hemizygous'.

questions.q: Why did only male fruit flies show white eyes in Morgan's initial crosses?
opts: The white eye allele is lethal in females.
The gene for eye color is on the Y chromosome.
The gene for eye color is X-linked, so males (XY) express the recessive trait with only one copy.
Male flies undergo more frequent mutations.
questions.exp: Option C is correct because X-linked eye color alleles are on the X chromosome; males have only one X chromosome (XY) and show the recessive eye color if that single chromosome carries the allele.
